derivations.claim: The grid has $d(d+1)$ horizontal and $d(d+1)$ vertical edges. Removing the $2d$ rough vertical edges leaves $n=2d^2$ physical edges. The grid has $(d+1)^2$ vertices, of which the two rough sides contain $2(d+1)$ distinct vertices; hence $Q_0$ has $(d-1)(d+1)=d^2-1$ coordinates. There are $d^2$ faces.

The columns of $\partial_2$ are independent. If a face combination $b\in Q_2$ has zero boundary, its coefficient on each top horizontal physical edge is the coefficient of the unique face immediately below that edge, so all top-row face coefficients vanish. On the next horizontal row, each boundary coefficient is the sum of the face coefficients immediately above and below; the already-zero top row forces the next row to vanish. Repeating downward gives $b=0$. Hence $\operatorname{rank}\partial_2=d^2$.

A self-avoiding left-to-right path starts with one of the $d+1$ horizontal edges from a left rough vertex into the patch. At each subsequent vertex the square grid has at most four incident edges, and the edge just used cannot be immediately traversed backwards, leaving at most three choices. Thus for length $\ell\ge1$ there are at most $(d+1)3^{\ell-1}\le(d+1)3^\ell$ such paths.

The rows of $\partial_1$ are independent. Indeed, a linear combination of rows with coefficients $a_v$ that vanishes on every physical edge has $a_u+a_v=0$ at the endpoints of each such edge, where $a_v=0$ on $R$. Every vertex outside $R$ is connected to $R$ by a horizontal path of physical edges, so these equations force every $a_v=0$.

For a finite binary matrix $A$ with $p$ independent rows, its map into $\mathbb F_2^p$ is onto. Otherwise its image is a proper subspace; by [F8], extend a basis of that image to a basis of $\mathbb F_2^p$ and choose an added basis vector $w$. Define a linear functional to be $1$ on $w$ and $0$ on every other vector of this basis. It is nonzero and vanishes on the image. In standard coordinates it is dot product with a nonzero coefficient vector, which gives a nontrivial linear combination of the rows of $A$ equal to zero, a contradiction. Thus the map rank is $p$. Apply this argument to $\partial_1$, using step 2.1, and to $\partial_2^{\mathsf T}$, whose rows are independent because they are the transposes of the independent columns of $\partial_2$ from step 1.2. Hence $\operatorname{rank}\partial_1=d^2-1$ and $\operatorname{rank}\partial_2^{\mathsf T}=d^2$; also $\operatorname{rank}\partial_2=d^2$ by the independent columns in step 1.2.

Put $C_2=\operatorname{row}(\partial_1)$ and $C_1=\ker(\partial_2^{\mathsf T})$. The chain identity from [[def-qc-square-planar-surface-code]] gives $C_2\subseteq C_1$. The independent rows in step 2.1 give $\dim C_2=d^2-1$, and [F5] with the map rank from step 3.1 gives $\dim C_1=2d^2-\operatorname{rank}(\partial_2^{\mathsf T})=d^2$. The CSS dimension theorem [F2] therefore gives $k=\dim C_1-\dim C_2=1$.

A Z-type Pauli with edge support $z$ commutes with every X check exactly when $\partial_1z=0$, so its support is a relative cycle. The Z-type stabilizers are exactly $\operatorname{im}\partial_2$, hence Z logical classes are $\ker\partial_1/\operatorname{im}\partial_2$. The chain identity gives $\operatorname{im}\partial_2\subseteq\ker\partial_1$. Extend a basis of $\operatorname{im}\partial_2$ to a basis of $\ker\partial_1$ using [F8]; the added basis vectors project to a basis of the quotient, since they span it and no nonzero combination of them lies in $\operatorname{im}\partial_2$. Therefore $\dim(\ker\partial_1/\operatorname{im}\partial_2)=\dim\ker\partial_1-\dim\operatorname{im}\partial_2$. By [F5], step 1.1 and step 3.1 give $\dim\ker\partial_1=n-\operatorname{rank}\partial_1=2d^2-(d^2-1)=d^2+1$ and $\dim\operatorname{im}\partial_2=\operatorname{rank}\partial_2=d^2$, so the quotient dimension is $1$.

For a relative cycle $z$, let $q_i(z)$ be the parity of its selected horizontal edges between columns $i$ and $i+1$, for $i=0,\ldots,d-1$. Summing the relative vertex-boundary equations over columns $1,\ldots,i$ cancels every interior edge twice and leaves only the two cut sets, so $q_0(z)=q_i(z)$. Each face boundary has either zero or two horizontal edges in a given column strip, so $q_i$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}\partial_2$. The straight horizontal row $z_0$ has $q_i(z_0)=1$ for every $i$, and is therefore not a relative boundary. Since the quotient in step 4.2 is one-dimensional, every nonzero Z logical class has all $q_i=1$; it must contain at least one horizontal edge in each of the $d$ disjoint strips. Thus its weight is at least $d$, and $z_0$ attains $d$.

In the edge subgraph of a relative cycle, every vertex outside $R$ has even degree, so all odd-degree vertices lie in $R$. The handshake identity $\sum_v\deg(v)=2|E|$ shows there are an even number of them. Add one dummy vertex joined to each odd boundary vertex; every degree in the augmented finite graph is now even. Starting with any unused edge, follow unused edges: at a vertex other than the start, the number of used incident edges is odd, so its even total degree leaves an unused edge. Finiteness therefore closes the trail at its start. Removing this closed trail preserves even degrees; repeating decomposes all edges into closed trails. Deleting dummy edges leaves cycles and paths with endpoints in $R$. Across any vertical cut, a cycle crosses evenly and a path crosses oddly exactly when its endpoints lie on opposite sides. Since $q_i=1$, at least one path joins the left and right rough sides. Removing repeated-vertex loops leaves a self-avoiding such path contained in the support. It crosses each of the $d$ disjoint vertical cuts, so its length is at least $d$.

For X-type supports, use the dual graph with one vertex per face and top and bottom exterior vertices, and one dual edge crossing each physical primal edge. The normalizer condition makes each face vertex even-degree, and X checks are the dual boundaries around vertices outside $R$. Their quotient has dimension $\dim(C_1/C_2)=1$ by step 4.1. A straight dual path from top to bottom is in the normalizer because it enters and leaves each face, and it crosses the straight Z logical row once. Since that Z cycle commutes with every X check, this odd intersection shows the dual path is not an X check; it represents the nonzero class.

For an X support $x$, let $q'_j(x)$ be the parity of selected horizontal primal edges in row $j$, for $j=0,\ldots,d$. Each X stabilizer has either zero or two such edges in each row, so every $q'_j$ vanishes on the X stabilizer space. The straight dual path from step 6.2 has $q'_j=1$ for all $j$. Since the X logical quotient is one-dimensional, every nontrivial class has $q'_j=1$ in each of the $d+1$ disjoint rows. Its weight is therefore at least $d+1$. In the dual support graph every face vertex has even degree, so the finite even-degree decomposition from the path argument in step 6.1, now with top and bottom exterior vertices as boundary vertices, splits it into cycles and paths ending at those exterior vertices. A cycle and a path with both endpoints at the same exterior vertex cross each horizontal cut evenly; since every $q'_j=1$, at least one path joins top to bottom. Every such path has length at least $d+1$, and the straight dual path attains this bound.

Step 5.1 and step 6.1 show that every nontrivial Z logical support contains a self-avoiding left-to-right path, so the path count bounds the number of candidate logical paths of each length. Step 5.1 and step 7.1 give minimum nontrivial Z and X logical weights $d$ and $d+1$, respectively. For a general normalizer Pauli $i^aX^xZ^z$, the CSS commutation equations require $X^x$ and $Z^z$ separately to normalize the checks. If both components are scalar-phase stabilizers then so is their product, so a nontrivial general class has at least one nontrivial component. Its physical support contains the support of each component, since an overlap gives a nonidentity $Y$ factor rather than cancellation. Thus its weight is at least $\min(d,d+1)=d$, and the straight Z row attains $d$. Since $k=1$ by step 4.1, [F4] gives stabilizer distance $d$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer code on $n$ qubits whose code space has dimension
$2^k$. The stabilizer **distance** is

$$d(S):=\min\{\operatorname{wt}(E):E\in N(S)\setminus Z_nS\}\quad\text{if }k>0.$$

This is a set difference: it excludes scalar-phase multiples of stabilizers.
If $k=0$, define $d(S)=+\infty$, since there is no nontrivial logical Pauli
class.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup generated by an ordered independent
Hermitian list $g_1,\ldots,g_r$. For a phase-aware Pauli error $E$, its
**syndrome** is the bit string $s(E)\in\mathbb F_2^r$ defined by

$$E g_j=(-1)^{s_j(E)}g_jE,\qquad s_j(E):=\omega(\lambda(E),\lambda(g_j)).$$

Here $\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$ is the binary Pauli label and
$\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'$. The scalar center of
$\mathcal P_n$ is $Z_n=\{i^kI:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$, and the
**normalizer** is $N(S)=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:Pg=gP\text{ for every }g\in S\}$.
The **logical Pauli classes** form the quotient group

$$N(S)/(Z_nS).$$

A normalizer element is logically nontrivial exactly when it lies in
$N(S)\setminus Z_nS$. Multiplication by a scalar phase does not change a
syndrome or logical class.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be an abelian subgroup of the Hermitian elements of
the phase-aware Pauli group $\mathcal P_n$ on the ordered $n$-qubit register.
Assume $-I\notin S$. The **stabilizer code space** is the common $+1$
eigenspace

$$\mathcal C(S):=\{\psi\in(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}:g\psi=\psi\text{ for every }g\in S\}.$$

If $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ are independent generators of $S$, the associated
stabilizer rank is $r$; independence means no nonempty product of distinct
generators is $I$. The code-space projector and its nonzero dimension are
established by [[thm-qc-stabilizer-projector-and-dimension]].

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be an abelian group of Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators with
$-I\notin S$, generated by $r$ independent checks. Then

$$P_S:=|S|^{-1}\sum_{g\in S}g$$

is the orthogonal projector onto the stabilizer code space and has rank
$2^{n-r}$. In particular, the code space is nonzero, including when $r=n$.

Let $V:H_L\to H_P$ be an isometry with $H_L\ne\{0\}$ and $P=VV^*$.
Let $\mathcal N(X)=\sum_{a=1}^m E_aXE_a^*$ be a finite Kraus
representation of a channel from $\mathcal B(H_P)$ to
$\mathcal B(H_O)$. If
$PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$ for all $a,b$, then there is a finite Kraus recovery
channel $\mathcal R:\mathcal B(H_O)\to\mathcal B(H_L)$ satisfying
$\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_V
=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_L)}$. It is obtained by diagonalizing $C$,
decoding each nonzero orthogonal error range, and sending the orthogonal
complement to a fixed logical state. For this recovery and every
$X\in\mathcal B(H_L)$, the off-diagonal error action is
$\mathcal R(E_aVX V^*E_b^*)=C_{ba}X$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Fix an ordered physical register $\mathcal H_P=\bigotimes_{j<n}\mathcal H_j$ with finite-dimensional factors. For $S\subseteq[n]:=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, form $\mathcal H_S$ and $\mathcal H_{S^c}$ in the inherited order, and let $\Pi_S:\mathcal H_P\to\mathcal H_S\otimes\mathcal H_{S^c}$ be the declared bijective wire permutation. An operator $E\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_P)$ is **supported in $S$** if there is $E_S\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_S)$ with

$$\Pi_S E\Pi_S^{-1}=E_S\otimes I_{S^c}.$$

Its **weight** is $\operatorname{wt}(E):=\min\{|S|:E\text{ is supported in }S\}$. The minimum exists because the full set $[n]$ supports every operator and $[n]$ has finitely many subsets. Let $\mathcal H_\varnothing=\mathbb C$; scalar identity operators have weight zero. The weight is invariant under reordering the tensor factors by their declared wire permutation ([[lem-qc-local-operator-support-is-permutation-invariant]]).

Here $E_S\otimes I_{S^c}$ is the tensor map of [[def-qc-tensor-map]]. The product factors may have arbitrary finite dimensions; qubits are the special case $\dim\mathcal H_j=2$ for every $j$.

derivations.claim: Let $E$ be a Pauli of weight less than $d(S)$. The code space is the common fixed space by [F3], and [F4] gives $P=Pg=gP$ for each $g\in S$. If $E$ anticommutes with some $g\in S$, then $PEP=PgEP=-PEgP=-PEP$ and hence $PEP=0$. If instead $E$ commutes with every $g$, then $E\in N(S)$. For $k>0$, its weight is below the minimum in [F1], forcing $E\in Z_nS$; for $k=0$, the same conclusion follows from $N(S)=Z_nS$. Writing $E=zs$ gives $PEP=zP$. Thus every such Pauli has scalar code-space compression, and every nonzero one not in the scalar-phase stabilizer is detected.

Enumerate the $m\ge1$ tensor Paulis of weight at most $t$ with factors in $\{I,X,Y,Z\}$ as $E_1,\ldots,E_m$; scalar phases do not affect correction. For any pair, the support of $E_a^*E_b$ lies in the union of their supports, so its weight is at most $2t<d(S)$. Step 1.1 gives $PE_a^*E_bP=C_{ab}P$ for a scalar $C_{ab}$. Let $V$ be the inclusion of the nonzero code space, so $P=VV^*$ by [F4]. Each $E_a$ is unitary by the matrices in [F6] and their tensor action [F7], so $F_a=E_a/\sqrt m$ are Kraus operators of the channel $\mathcal N(A)=m^{-1}\sum_a E_aAE_a^*$: each summand is a unitary conjugation and $\sum_aF_a^*F_a=I$. Applying [F5] to $PF_a^*F_bP=(C_{ab}/m)P$ gives a recovery $\mathcal R$. Its off-diagonal formula gives $\mathcal R(E_aVX V^*E_a^*)=C_{aa}X=X$, since $E_a^*E_a=I$. Thus this single recovery corrects every Pauli in the family.

On one qubit every matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ has the expansion $A=\frac{a+d}{2}I+\frac{b+c}{2}X+\frac{c-b}{2i}Y+\frac{a-d}{2}Z$, as direct substitution of [F6] verifies. In the ordered one-qubit basis, the matrix units satisfy $|0\rangle\langle0|=(I+Z)/2$, $|1\rangle\langle1|=(I-Z)/2$, $|0\rangle\langle1|=(X+iY)/2$, and $|1\rangle\langle0|=(X-iY)/2$. For bit strings $a,b\in\{0,1\}^n$, [F7] identifies the global matrix unit $|a\rangle\langle b|$ with the tensor product of the corresponding one-qubit matrix units, so each global matrix unit is a linear combination of tensor Pauli operators. Every endomorphism has its matrix-unit expansion $A=\sum_{a,b}\langle A e_b,e_a\rangle\,|a\rangle\langle b|$ in this ordered computational basis; hence tensor Pauli operators span the full operator space. An operator supported on a fixed set of at most $t$ qubits is a linear combination of the tensor Paulis that are identity off that set, so each term has weight at most $t$. For Kraus operators $K_\mu=\sum_a u_{\mu a}E_a$ in the stated span, $PK_\mu^*K_\nu P=\bigl(\sum_{a,b}\overline{u_{\mu a}}u_{\nu b}C_{ab}\bigr)P$ by step 2.1. The code is nonzero by [F4], so [F5] applies to this actual finite channel and gives exact recovery.
